question: In rectangle \(PQRS,\) \(PQ = 8\) and \(QR = 6.\) Points \(A\) and \(B\) lie on \(PQ,\) points \(C\) and \(D\) lie on \(QR,\) points \(E\) and \(F\) lie on \(RS,\) and points \(G\) and \(H\) lie on \(SP\) so that \(AP = BQ < 4\) and the convex octagon \(ABCDEFGH\) is equilateral. The length of a side of this octagon can be expressed in the form \(k + m\sqrt{n},\) where \(k,\) \(m,\) and \(n\) are integers and \(n\) is not divisible by the square of any prime. What is \(k + m + n?\)
solution:
The equality \(AP=BQ\) lets us compare corner triangles and prove that \(CD\) is centered on \(QR\).

Let the common octagon side length be \(2x\). Because \(AP=BQ<4\), the order on \(PQ\) is \(P,A,B,Q\), so
\[
AP=BQ=\frac{8-2x}{2}=4-x.
\]
The right triangles \(APH\) and \(BQC\) have equal hypotenuses \(AH=BC\) and equal legs \(AP=BQ\). By hypotenuse-leg congruence, \(PH=QC\).

The boundary orders on the other two sides are \(P,H,G,S\) and \(Q,C,D,R\). Since \(HG=CD=2x\),
\[
PG=PH+HG=QC+CD=QD.
\]
Subtracting these equal lengths from \(PS=QR=6\) gives \(SG=RD\).

Now the right triangles \(FSG\) and \(ERD\) have equal hypotenuses \(FG=ED\) and equal legs \(SG=RD\). Thus \(SF=RE\). Since \(EF=2x\) and \(SR=8\),
\[
SF=RE=4-x=BQ.
\]
Consequently, the right triangles \(ERD\) and \(BQC\) are also congruent by hypotenuse-leg, giving \(RD=QC\). Using \(QR=QC+CD+DR=6\), we obtain
\[
QC=RD=3-x.
\]
Apply the Pythagorean theorem to \(BQC\):
\[
(4-x)^2+(3-x)^2=(2x)^2.
\]
Expanding and collecting terms gives
\[
25-14x+2x^2=4x^2,
\qquad 2x^2+14x-25=0.
\]
The quadratic formula yields
\[
x=\frac{-14\pm\sqrt{196+200}}{4}
=\frac{-7\pm3\sqrt{11}}{2}.
\]
Because \(x>0\), the octagon side length is \(2x=-7+3\sqrt{11}\). Thus \(k=-7\), \(m=3\), and \(n=11\), giving
\[
k+m+n=-7+3+11=\boxed{7}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{B}\).
